english.title: Use threatening / abusive / insulting words / behaviour to cause harassment / alarm / distress
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), with intent to cause **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) harassment, alarm or distress, used threatening, abusive or insulting words or behaviour or disorderly behaviour, thereby causing that person or another harassment, alarm or distress
english.legislation: Contrary to Section 4A(1) and (5) of the Public Order Act 1986.

english.notes:
(i) Where the specific date of the offence is not known, the charge should read: "...on a date between X and Y...". where 'X' is the last date before the first date on which the offence could have occurred, and 'Y' is the first date after the last date it could have occurred.
(e.g. a factory closes Friday evening to Monday morning. It is broken into over the weekend. The charge should read: "...on a date between X (Thursday's date) and Y (Tuesday's date)...".)
(ii) Practical Considerations:
(a) 'Threatening' includes verbal and physical threats and violent conduct
'Abusive' means degrading or reviling language
'Insulting' means scornful, insolent, contemptuous
(b) There must be evidence that the suspect actually intended to cause harassment, alarm or distress, not merely that that was the consequence of his behaviour.
(c) There must be evidence that harassment, alarm or distress was actually caused.
(d) This offence is not commonly used because it is usually easier to prove Section 5 Public Order Act 1986.
(iii) Where there is no evidence of intent or actual causation of harassment, alarm or distress, consider section 5 Public Order Act.
(iv) Where the extent of the behaviour results in the fear or realisation of violence, consider section 4(1) of the Act or assault charges.
(v) Where there is repeated harassment of individuals, consider the definition of "harassment" and the offence as provided by sections 1 and 2 sections 1 and 2 respectively of the Protection from Harassment Act 1997.
(vi) See also offence wording: H351 - relating to writing, signs and visible representation.
(VII)See the CPS charging standards for this offence before preparing any charges.

Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.
